title: Rust: Unit Tests
description: Write unit tests using Rust's built-in testing framework.

steps.title: Simple Test Function
steps.description: Write a function `add(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32` and a test `#[test] fn test_add()` that asserts `add(2, 3) == 5`. Print "Tests passed!" in main.
hints: Run tests with the test runner concept.
In a normal project, `cargo test` would run these.

verification.failureMessage: Define a test for add(2,3) and print the result.

steps.title: Multiple Test Cases
steps.description: Write a function `factorial(n: u32) -> u32` with multiple tests: test(0)=1, test(1)=1, test(5)=120. Print all results.
hints: Add several tests in the tests module.

steps.title: Test-Driven Development (TDD)
steps.description: Practice TDD: write a test first for a function `is_even(n: i32) -> bool` (test even gets true, odd gets false), then implement the function to pass the tests.
hints: Then implement: `fn is_even(n: i32) -> bool { n % 2 == 0 }`
Run tests to verify they pass.

verification.failureMessage: Write a failing test first, then implement is_even.

steps.title: Test with Expected Panic
steps.description: Write a function `divide(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64` that panics on division by zero. Write a test `#[test] #[should_panic(expected = "division by zero")]`.
hints: Test both valid division and panic case.

verification.failureMessage: Test division by zero panics and valid division works.

steps.title: Test Organization
steps.description: Organize tests into submodules: `mod tests { mod math_tests { ... } mod string_tests { ... } }`. Write tests for math functions and string functions in separate modules.
hints: This mirrors how real Rust projects organize tests.

verification.failureMessage: Create math_tests and string_tests submodules with tests.
